intended_use: Compute claimed score from parsed QSOs in SH6.
sources_note: Rules summarized from official contest pages discovered during parallel research. Some contests need annual refresh before strict production scoring.

band_scope_terms.per_band_per_mode: Counted separately on each band and each mode

score_patterns.distance: final_score primarily derived from distance/km model

rule_sets.name: CQ World Wide DX Contest (CW/SSB)

rules.notes: North America intra-continental exception may score 2 in rulebook edge cases.
QSO may still be valid for multiplier credit depending on contest rules.

key_variants: CW and SSB weekends share scoring model.
Maritime mobile entries may have special multiplier handling.

rule_sets.name: CQ WW RTTY
notes: W/VE QTH includes US states/DC and VE areas as defined by rules.

rule_sets.name: CQ 160 (CW/SSB)
key_variants: CW and SSB are separate events but share the same scoring model.

rule_sets.name: CQ World Wide VHF Contest
notes: Four-character worked grids count once per band for fixed stations.
Including the sent grid in multiplier and duplicate identity implements the official rover rule when the rover changes grid location.
The 2026 contest has separate analog and digital weekends, but both use this scoring model.

rule_sets.name: World Wide Digi DX Contest
notes: Each QSO scores one point plus one point for each 3,000 km between four-character grid-square centers.
A station may be worked once per band, either FT4 or FT8; mode does not create a second scoring QSO.
Two-character grid fields count once on each band.

rule_sets.name: FT8 DX Contest
notes: Each QSO scores one point plus one point for each 3,000 km between four-character grid-square centers.
A station may be worked once per band; only FT8 contacts on 80, 40, 20, 15, and 10 metres are eligible.
Two-character grid fields count once on each band.
This current rule materially differs from LogChecker's recovered legacy implementation, which used flat one-point QSOs and global U.S.-state, Canadian-province, and other-DXCC multipliers.

rule_sets.name: JARL World Wide RTTY Contest
notes: JARL assumed responsibility for the former JARTS contest beginning with the 2026 event.
Same-continent contacts, including the same DXCC entity, score two points; cross-continent contacts score three.
Maritime-mobile contacts score two points regardless of location and do not count as multipliers.
DXCC entities other than mainland JA/W/VE/VK count once per band; mainland JA/W/VE/VK instead count by portable-aware call area once per band.
The received age (or permitted 00/01/99 substitute) must be present; organizer adjudication of its semantic validity remains authoritative.

rule_sets.name: International FT Challenge
notes: The organizer replaced the FT Roundup (whose Cabrillo identifier was FT8-RU) with the International FT Challenge in 2024 after materially changing its rules.
Each QSO scores one point plus one point for each 3,000 km between four-character grid-square centers; a missing received grid defaults to ZZ00 and scores one point only.
ZZ is not a multiplier. Two-character grid fields count once per band, and a call may be worked once per band across FT4 and FT8.
Only the first 24 operating hours count. Gaps of at least 30 minutes with no logged QSOs are excluded from accumulated operating time.
The current organizer page is headed for the 5-6 December 2026 event although two administrative date examples in the body still show 2025; the scoring clauses are unambiguous.

rule_sets.name: Japan International DX Contest — CW
notes: Only JA-to-DX (including maritime mobile) and DX-to-JA contacts score; JA-to-JA, DX-to-DX, and DX-to-maritime-mobile contacts do not.
Band points are 4 on 160 m, 2 on 80 m and 10 m, and 1 on 40 m, 20 m, and 15 m.
JA entrants count received CQ zones and non-JD1 DXCC entities per band; maritime mobile supplies only a zone multiplier.
DX and maritime-mobile entrants count received Japanese prefecture numbers 01-50 per band; 48-50 represent the three JD1 island multipliers.

rule_sets.name: Japan International DX Contest — Phone
notes: This is the phone event corresponding to jidx_cw; scoring and multipliers are identical, but only phone modes are eligible.
The official 2025-04 revision explicitly publishes the 2026 CW and phone schedules.

rule_sets.name: IG-RY World Wide RTTY Contest
notes: Each valid contact scores one point; the same station may be worked once per band.
Each different four-digit year of the operator's first official amateur-radio licence counts once per band.
Single operators may use 24 of the 30 hours; gaps of at least 60 minutes with no QSO are excluded from accumulated operating time. Multi-operator stations may use all 30 hours.

The organizer requires at least ten minutes before changing bands, including single operators, but defines no per-QSO scoring penalty for a violation. SH6 records this as an adjudication/compliance requirement and does not invent one.

rule_sets.name: Oceania DX Contest — CW
notes: The organizer's 2026 announcement confirms the event dates and scoring structure; the latest detailed official rule PDF is the 2025 edition and supplies the unchanged prefix definitions and exchange details.
Oceania entrants may work any station; entrants outside Oceania score only contacts with Oceania stations.
QSO points are 20 on 160 m, 10 on 80 m, 5 on 40 m, 1 on 20 m, 2 on 15 m, and 3 on 10 m.
Portable-aware amateur-radio prefixes count once per band. A missing received serial is logged as 001 under the official rule and therefore is not silently rejected by SH6.

rule_sets.name: Oceania DX Contest — Phone
notes: This is the phone event corresponding to oceania_dx_cw; scoring and multiplier behavior are identical, but only phone modes are eligible.

rule_sets.name: GACW WWSA CW DX Contest — recovered legacy scoring
rule_sets.rules_year: legacy recovered behavior; current official rules not verified
notes: This rule is explicitly legacy-compatible, not a claim about the current organizer rules. Organizer sites and web search were unreachable during the 2026-08-26 research pass.

The behavior is ported from LogChecker's fixture-backed gacw-recovered rule: zero points for the same DXCC entity, one point for another entity on the same continent, three points across continents, and five points when the worked station is in South America.

Received CQ zones and resolved DXCC entities count separately on each band. Mobile and maritime-mobile stations receive no multiplier credit. The recovered implementation performs no duplicate elimination.
A later switch to verified current official rules may be material and must be implemented as a separately versioned rule or reviewed before changing this legacy scorer.

rule_sets.name: HA-DX Contest
notes: The current official 2026 rules award 10 points for a Hungarian station, 2 points for another station on the entrant's continent, and 5 points for another continent. Aeronautical- and maritime-mobile contacts score 2 points and do not multiply.
Hungarian counties and non-Hungarian DXCC/WAE-list countries count once per band regardless of mode. The 20 official county abbreviations are validated.
In MIX categories the same station may be worked once per band in each of CW and SSB; other categories allow it once per band. When CATEGORY-MODE is absent SH6 conservatively applies once per band.

Current scoring differs materially from LogChecker's recovered 1/3/5 and 1/3/6 entrant-dependent point tables, entrant-dependent multiplier sets, minimum-one multiplier, and lack of duplicate elimination.

Limitation: SH6 resolves ordinary DXCC entities, but it does not yet distinguish WAE-only subentities that share a DXCC entity. Logs relying on such a WAE-only multiplier can be undercounted. Adjudication penalties, cross-log validation, and multi-operator 10-minute compliance are outside claimed-score computation.

rule_sets.name: USKA Helvetia Contest
notes: The March 2026 official rules award 10 points for a valid Swiss contact, 1 point within the entrant's continent, and 3 points outside it.
Swiss stations must send one of 26 canton abbreviations; other stations must send a serial of at least three digits. Incomplete or incorrect exchanges score zero.
Each callsign may be worked once per band in CW, once in SSB, and once in the combined digital mode group. Cantons and DXCC countries, including Switzerland, count independently per band.
The 2026 rules add digital operation and explicit duplicate and exchange validation to the fixture-backed recovered behavior. LogChecker's recovered point and multiplier values otherwise agree.

The required six-hour single-operator rest period, team-member cross-log exclusion, and adjudication sanctions are compliance checks rather than deterministic claimed-score branches and are not inferred from a single submitted QSO list.

rule_sets.name: World Wide Holyland DX Contest
rule_sets.rules_year: 2025 detailed official rules; 2026 event endpoint and exchange confirmed
notes: IARC's April 2025 bulletin is the latest complete organizer rule text retrieved. The official IARC 2026 endpoint listed by ARRL was unreachable during retrieval, while the 2026 calendar confirms the same five bands, CW/phone modes, and Israeli-area-or-serial exchange.

Outside-Israel entrants score 8 points for Israel, 1 for their own DXCC entity, 2 for another entity on the same continent, and 4 across continents. Israeli entrants score 1 for Israel, 2 for other Asian stations, and 8 for other continents. /MM contacts score 4 for everyone and do not multiply.
Israeli stations must send a five-character Holyland area such as H08HF; other stations must send a serial beginning at 001. Each DXCC entity and valid Israeli area count separately per band.
Duplicates are once per callsign, band, and CW/phone mode. Israeli mobile location suffixes remain part of the callsign, matching the official distinct-location treatment.
Cross-log errors, the multioperator ten-minute rule, and the half-hour minimum at each Israeli mobile area require adjudication evidence and are not inferred by claimed-score computation.

rule_sets.name: North American QSO Party — CW
notes: A valid complete exchange scores one point. At least one side of every valid QSO must be a North American entity under the ARRL DXCC list, with Hawaii added explicitly.

Multipliers per band are all 50 states, DC, 13 Canadian provinces/territories, and other North American DXCC entities. Non-North-American stations and /MM or /AM stations can score QSO credit but never multiply.

Single operators may operate 10 of 12 hours; a gap between QSO timestamps must be at least 31 minutes to contain the required 30 intervening off-time minutes. M2 entries may use the full period and SH6 applies the 10-minute transmitter band lock when TX_ID is present.

LogChecker's recovered rule omitted duplicates, mode/band restrictions, exchange/geography eligibility, and operating limits, and incorrectly normalized Maryland (MD) to District of Columbia (DC). SH6 keeps MD and DC distinct under the official rules.

rule_sets.name: North American QSO Party — SSB
notes: Uses the same 2026 scoring, exchanges, multipliers, duplicate policy, and operating limits as naqp_cw_2026, with phone modes only.

rule_sets.name: North American QSO Party — RTTY
notes: Uses the same 2026 scoring, exchanges, multipliers, duplicate policy, and operating limits as naqp_cw_2026, but permits RTTY only and excludes 160 metres.

rule_sets.name: RAC Canada Day and Canada Winter Contests
notes: The official 2026 document defines identical scoring for Canada Day and Canada Winter: listed RAC official stations score 20 points, other Canadian stations including VE0 score 10, and stations outside Canada score 2.
Canadian stations send one of 13 province/territory abbreviations; VE0 and stations outside Canada send a serial. Each province/territory counts once per band and CW/phone mode group.
A callsign may be worked once in each mode group on each of eight bands from 160 m through 2 m. If no Canadian multiplier is worked, the official minimum multiplier of one is applied.

For MOST logs, SH6 enforces transmitter-specific 10-minute band locks and the multiplier-station new-multiplier restriction when Cabrillo TX_ID data is present; otherwise the unverified operational constraint is reported.
LogChecker's recovered scorer omitted duplicate, band/mode, exchange, minimum-multiplier, and multioperator constraints and treated all non-CW modes as multiplier-eligible.

rule_sets.name: PACC Contest
notes: Every valid QSO involving a Dutch station scores one point. Non-Dutch entrants may score only Dutch contacts; Dutch entrants may also claim cross-contest contacts when a serial is received.
Dutch stations send one of the 12 official province abbreviations and other stations send a serial. The same call may be worked once per band in CW and once in SSB.

Non-Dutch entrants multiply Dutch provinces; Dutch entrants multiply DXCC entities except that Asiatic Russia, Chile, Japan, Argentina, Brazil, Canada, the USA, Australia, South Africa, and New Zealand use the official callsign-area identities. All multipliers count independently per band and mode.

Current official rules differ from LogChecker's recovered scorer by making multipliers per band and mode, enforcing duplicates, bands, modes, and exchanges, and treating Dutch-to-foreign cross-contest serial contacts explicitly as valid.

Special callsigns whose call area cannot be derived from their visible callsign, SWL-specific scoring, cross-log penalties, and multioperator category reclassification require organizer or external evidence and are not inferred by claimed-score computation. Ordinary and explicit portable/reciprocal call-area designators are supported.

rule_sets.name: A.R.I. International DX Contest
notes: For non-Italian entrants, an Italian contact scores 10 points, another country on the same continent scores 1, another continent scores 3, and an own-country contact scores zero but can still multiply. Italian entrants score 1 for Europe and 3 outside Europe; Italian-to-Italian QSOs are forbidden and receive no credit.

Italian stations send one of the 107 official province abbreviations and other stations send a serial. A callsign may be worked once per band in each of CW, SSB, and RTTY, while a multiplier counts only once per band regardless of mode.
Outside entrants count Italian provinces plus non-Italian DXCC/WAE entities. Italian entrants count non-Italian DXCC/WAE entities. I, IS, and IT9 are excluded as country multipliers.

The official 2026 rules differ from LogChecker's recovered behavior by forbidding Italian-to-Italian QSOs, adding the SU province, and enforcing current exchanges, five bands, three modes, duplicates, and mode-independent per-band multiplier scope.

Limitation: SH6 resolves ordinary DXCC entities but does not distinguish WAE-only subentities that share a DXCC entity, so those multipliers can be undercounted. SWL scoring, cross-log adjudication, and Multi-One ten-minute violations require evidence outside a single claimed-score log.

rule_sets.name: AEGEAN-RTTY legacy-compatible scoring
notes: No current or archived organizer rule page could be verified during this research pass. This rule is an explicit fixture-backed compatibility port of LogChecker's recovered aegean.dll behavior and must not be represented as current organizer-authoritative scoring.
Same-continent contacts score 3 points on 160/80/40 metres and 1 point on 20/15/10 metres. Cross-continent contacts score 6 on 80/40, 2 on 20/15/10, and zero on 160 metres.
A worked /QRP suffix doubles the QSO value; worked SV5, SV8, or SV9 calls triple it, and the factors compound. An entrant callsign containing /QRP adds 20 points once to the final score.

The recovered DLL does not eliminate duplicates and contains no explicit mode or exchange validation, so this compatibility rule deliberately retains those limitations. Calls without resolvable country/continent data score zero conservatively.

rule_sets.name: AEGEAN-VHF legacy-compatible scoring
notes: No current or archived organizer rule page could be verified during this research pass. This rule is an explicit fixture-backed compatibility port of LogChecker's recovered aegvhf.dll behavior and must not be represented as current organizer-authoritative scoring.

Each QSO contributes the locator distance rounded up to the next whole kilometre; a same-four-character-grid QSO contributes one point. Missing or malformed locator distance contributes zero points rather than being guessed.
For each band separately, the recovered DLL multiplies the number of QSO rows by the sum of QSO point values and by the number of unique received four-character grids, then sums those band products.
The recovered DLL retains duplicate rows and contains no explicit band, mode, or exchange-validity gate beyond locator extraction. This compatibility rule deliberately retains those limitations.

rule_sets.name: Africa All Mode International DX Contest 2026
notes: The current SARL 2026 rules award one point to every valid QSO and multiply by the sum of unique African DXCC entities worked separately on each band and in each of CW and SSB.

A station may be worked once per band per mode. A complete received exchange must contain RS(T) and an incremental serial; SH6 validates the received serial represented by its exchange field but cannot cross-check the other station's transmitted sequence from a single log.

Ship-based and aeronautical calls score one point but never count as multipliers. SH6 identifies African entities using the contest-time cty.dat continent classification, corresponding to the official ARRL AF-DXCC definition.

This differs materially from LogChecker's recovered afdx.dll behavior, which awards two points for African contacts and also separates an unsupported third mode group. The SH6 rule follows the current organizer rules instead. Certificate eligibility, cross-mode/cross-band contact validity, and adjudication penalties require evidence beyond a single submitted log.

rule_sets.name: AGB-PARTY latest organizer-published scoring
rule_sets.rules_year: latest organizer page dated 2022; event still listed in 2024-2025 calendars
notes: The latest live AGB organizer page is dated for the 16 December 2022 edition, while independent 2024 and 2025 calendars continue to list the event and organizer. No newer organizer rule revision was found, so this explicitly versioned rule uses the latest organizer-published format rather than silently presenting it as a 2026 rule.

On 40 and 80 metres, a non-FT contact with an AGB member number in the received exchange scores 5 points; another nonmember on the entrant's continent scores 1 and a nonmember on another continent scores 3. FT4 and FT8 contacts use their normal exchange and score 1 point.

The same station may be worked once in each exact mode during each 15-minute period. Each distinct DXCC/WAE country and each received AGB member number counts once for the whole contest; the final score is total QSO points times their combined count.

This differs from LogChecker's recovered DLL by adding the current 40-metre band, digital and FT modes, the 15-minute exact-mode duplicate rule, and current exchange handling. Limitation: SH6 resolves ordinary DXCC entities but cannot distinguish WAE-only subentities sharing a DXCC entity, so country multipliers can be undercounted. Missing timestamps cannot be safely assigned to a 15-minute period and are conservatively treated as distinct rows rather than guessed.

rule_sets.name: Asia-Pacific Sprint 2026
notes: The organizer's January 2024 revision, updated with the June 2026 schedule, defines three editions: February on 20/40 metres CW, June on 15/20 metres SSB, and October on 15/20 metres CW. SH6 selects the edition from each QSO's UTC date rather than applying one band's rules to every historical log.

Asia-Pacific entrants may work any station; entrants elsewhere score only contacts with the organizer's explicit Asia-Pacific entity list. Each accepted QSO is one point, a station may be worked once per band, and WPX prefixes count once for the entire contest. A numeric received serial is required.

The implementation uses explicit callsign and DXCC-entity handling for UA0 but not UA9, VK1-9 except VK9X/VK9Y, and ZL excluding Chatham and Kermadec, plus every other entity enumerated by the organizer. This matches LogChecker's recovered eligibility and global-prefix model while adding current schedule, exchange, mode, band, and duplicate enforcement.

Limitation: the called station must QSY at least 1 kHz after CW QSOs or 6 kHz after SSB QSOs. A single Cabrillo log does not reliably identify which party was called or prove subsequent transmissions, so SH6 cannot adjudicate that operating rule. Russian and Belarusian submitted logs are organizer checklogs from October 2023 onward; SH6 computes their claimed score but does not determine award eligibility.

rule_sets.name: Contest delle Sezioni A.R.I. 2026
notes: The official 2026 rules admit Italian ARI members operating from Italian territory with ordinary I-prefixed licence calls, plus IQ section stations. Special prefixes and Italian stations operating abroad are excluded. SH6 enforces Italian entity and ordinary/IQ callsign shape, but ARI membership and the licensed-versus-special status of unusual calls require organizer records and remain an adjudication limitation.

Valid contacts use 160 through 10 metres excluding WARC, with RTTY limited to 80 through 10 metres. A call may be worked once per band in each CW, SSB, and RTTY mode. Points are 3 on 160, 2 on 80, 1 on 40, 2 on 20, 3 on 15, and 4 on 10 metres.
The received exchange must be an ordinary three-character ASC section code. Each section counts once per band and mode; the final score is total QSO points times their combined count.

This supersedes LogChecker's recovered legacy behavior, which uses old four-digit section codes and the former 2/2/1/3/5/5 band table. SH6 validates the current ASC syntax but cannot prove that a syntactically valid code was active on the contest date without a versioned organizer dataset, so the rule is marked partial. Digital mode grouping is restricted by the point model to RTTY-compatible Cabrillo modes.

rule_sets.name: Araucaria VHF Contest legacy-compatible scoring
rule_sets.rules_year: archived rules, circa 2017; current organizer status unverified
notes: No current organizer rule publication could be verified. The former avhfc.com domain now serves unrelated content, while the latest organizer-linked material found is archived historical material. This rule is therefore explicitly legacy-compatible and must not be read as a current AVHFC rule.

The fixture-backed recovered behavior awards one base point on 6 metres and two on 2 metres, counts unique normalized received locators per band, retains all duplicate rows, and adds one point for identical normalized locators or the floor of the derived distance in kilometres otherwise.

The final score is the sum, for each band, of base QSO points times unique received locators, plus all whole-kilometre distance bonuses. Four-character locators use the recovered 55AA expansion, values longer than six characters are truncated to six, and text after a comma is ignored.

Archived published rules describe the same point branches and bandwise grid-plus-distance formula, but organizer cross-log validity and category/award rules are outside a single-log score computation.

rule_sets.name: 61st Baltic Contest 2026
notes: The official LRSF 2026 rules use 80 metres only: CW from 3510 through 3600 kHz and SSB from 3600 through 3750 kHz. The exchange is RS(T) plus a serial starting at 001, and each station may be worked once in each mode.

Baltic entrants in Estonia, Latvia, or Lithuania score one point for European QSOs and two for other continents. Other European entrants score ten for Baltic QSOs and one otherwise; entrants outside Europe score twenty for Baltic QSOs and one otherwise. The final score is the sum of QSO points with no multiplier.
In accordance with the explicit 2026 LRSF decision, QSOs involving Russia or Belarus score zero. SH6 uses resolved country and ordinary ES/YL/LY callsign identity.

LogChecker's recovered geography branches agree with the current point table but count every parsed row. SH6 additionally enforces the official numeric exchange, frequency/mode limits, once-per-mode duplicate rule, and 2026 Russia/Belarus exclusion. Exact frequency is required rather than assuming an in-band value from a band label.

rule_sets.name: ARI Basso Ferrarese legacy-compatible scoring
rule_sets.rules_year: unverified historical event; fixture-backed recovered behavior
notes: No current or archived organizer rule publication could be verified. Contemporary N1MM documentation still lists the ARI Basso Ferrarese user-defined contest but provides no sponsor rules. This rule is therefore explicitly legacy-compatible and not represented as current organizer scoring.

The fixture-backed recovered DLL accepts only 40- and 20-metre rows. Ordinary contacts score one point; the embedded Jolly calls IQ4FF, I4JEE, IZ4OSH, IK4RDP, IZ4ISC, and IZ4SJI score 100 points and each count as a Jolly occurrence on that band.

For each band, its QSO points are multiplied by 100 times the number of Jolly QSOs, or by one when none were logged; band results are then added. The recovered module retains repeated contacts, including repeated Jolly calls.

The unusual repeated-Jolly multiplication is intentionally preserved exactly from LogChecker's fixture-backed implementation. Without organizer rules, SH6 does not infer mode, exchange, date, participant geography, or duplicate restrictions.

rule_sets.name: BDM WW RTTY legacy-compatible scoring
rule_sets.rules_year: historical event documented 2013-2020; fixture-backed recovered scoring
notes: No current organizer source could be verified. Historical announcements document BDM WW RTTY editions from 2013 through at least 2020, while the original organizer pages are unavailable. This rule is explicitly legacy-compatible rather than current.

The fixture-backed recovered DLL awards five points when the station and worked station are on the same continent and ten points when they are on different continents. Unresolved geography scores zero; there is no multiplier and the final score is the point sum.

Historical announcements describe RTTY, five HF bands, numeric serials, and once-per-band contacts, but these constraints are not present in LogChecker's recovered scoring fixture. SH6 does not graft an unversioned secondary-source event format onto the recovered rule and therefore retains every parsed row exactly as the DLL did.

rule_sets.name: California QSO Party 2026
notes: The official 2026 rules award three points for every complete non-duplicate CW or phone QSO, a change from the two-point phone rule used through 2025 and by LogChecker's recovered module. Six HF bands are eligible and a station may be worked once per band in each mode.

California entrants work everyone and count US states plus all 13 Canadian provinces/territories once globally, capped at 58 scored multipliers; the first California county worked supplies the California multiplier and DX supplies QSO credit only. Other entrants work California only and count its 58 counties globally.

The exchange must contain a numeric serial plus an official location. SH6 identifies a California entrant from the official county sent in its Cabrillo exchanges, supports multiple counties in a county-line exchange, and treats a mobile changing county or state as a new duplicate identity. Duplicate contacts score zero but may still supply new multiplier credit, as the organizer explicitly permits.

Single-operator and assisted entries are limited to the first 24 operating hours with breaks of at least 15 minutes. Multi-operator operator-replacement timing, transmitter concurrency, spotting, physical-location, and audio-based adjudication cannot be proven from ordinary Cabrillo QSO rows, so this rule is marked partial.

rule_sets.name: CIS DX QPSK63 legacy-compatible scoring
rule_sets.rules_year: historical event documented 2009-2013; fixture-backed recovered scoring
notes: No current organizer rules or edition could be verified. The former cisdx.srars.org site is unavailable, historical organizer material documents the event in 2009, and published result records were found through 2013. This rule is explicitly legacy-compatible rather than current.

The fixture-backed recovered DLL awards three points to calls matching its embedded CIS-prefix fragments and one point to other calls, excluding /M and /MM suffixes and the Antarctic R1AN/RI1AN patterns. It retains duplicate rows.

Each distinct non-empty received exchange counts once globally, except exchanges containing the literal placeholder 0000. The recovered case-sensitive comparison behavior is preserved. Historical organizer material also required QPSK63 and at most 100 W, but those constraints are not inferable reliably from ordinary parsed QSO rows and are not grafted onto the recovered scorer.

rule_sets.name: CQ-M International DX Contest 2025
notes: The latest official CQ-M rules published by the organizer are the 2025 edition. They award two points within a continent while treating Europe and Asia together as Eurasia, and three points between other continents. This replaces LogChecker's recovered one-point same-entity and same-Russian-region branches.

CW and phone contacts on 160, 80, 40, 20, 15, and 10 metres require a numeric progressive serial. A station may be worked once per band in each mode. R-150-S countries and territories count once per band, and /MM contacts supply no multiplier.

SH6 uses its resolved country/entity identity plus the recovered Russian R1N/R4/R6/R9/R0 territory splits that remain present in the current official R-150-S list. It cannot prove progressive serial ordering, one-signal operation, remote-receiver, self-spotting, or organizer cross-log confirmation from a single ordinary log, so the rule is marked partial.

rule_sets.name: CQMM DX Contest 2026
notes: The organizer announces the 18-19 April 2026 event and describes its logger support as updated for the 2025/2026 rules. CQMM DX is the current international continuation of the historical CWJF Manchester Mineira contest represented by LogChecker's CWJF-MM identifier.

Ordinary same-entity contacts score one point. Different entities on the same continent score two points on 20/15/10 metres and four on 80/40; different continents score three and six respectively. A valid exchange ending C, M, Q, or Y scores ten points, while /MM scores three. CW only is permitted on 80 through 10 metres, and each call may be worked once per band.

Every DXCC entity counts once globally and every South American WPX prefix counts separately on each band. SH6 encodes the band in the South-American multiplier identity while retaining global DXCC identity. It cannot prove category, power, single-signal, operator, self-spotting, or organizer cross-log requirements from an ordinary single log, so the rule is marked partial.

rule_sets.name: DIG QSO Party HF (rules valid since 2025)
notes: The official rules valid since 2025 define separate SSB and CW parties on the second full weekends of March and April. Saturday covers exact 20/15/10-metre segments from 1200-1700 UTC; Sunday covers exact 80-metre segments from 0700-0900 and 40-metre segments from 0900-1100 UTC. SH6 validates mode, date, time, and exact frequency for each row.

A claimed DIG member number scores ten points; a non-member exchange scores one. Each call may be worked once per band. Each claimed DIG number counts once globally, while every DXCC or WAE country counts once per band. The final score multiplies points by the sum of both multiplier families.

SH6 can validate the form of a claimed membership number but cannot prove that it belonged to the worked callsign on the contest date. Its normal entity resolver also cannot distinguish every WAE-only entity sharing a DXCC identity. Those limitations make this rule partial; it does not silently invent member or WAE data.

rule_sets.name: DARC Christmas Contest 2025
notes: The current DARC contest hub and 2025 results confirm one point per valid QSO and the final formula QSO points multiplied by the sum of DOK and WPX-prefix multipliers. The annual contest runs on 26 December from 0830 through 1059 UTC on 80 and 40 metres in CW and SSB.

German DARC/VFDB members send a DOK, German non-members send NM, and stations outside Germany send a progressive serial. A station may be worked once per band. In Mixed entries, multiplier identities are counted separately by band and by CW/SSB; SH6 applies that scope consistently.

SH6 conservatively recognizes only ordinary one-letter/two-digit DOKs because no redistributable, versioned special-DOK list was found. It cannot prove whether a CQ-calling station changed frequency after each QSO, progressive-serial ordering, transmitter/category restrictions, or organizer cross-log validation from one ordinary log, so the rule is partial. LogChecker's recovered dxmas.dll instead retains all duplicate rows, accepts a defective three-character DOK test, omits the contest window and exchange rules, and does not separate multipliers by mode.

rule_sets.name: European PSK DX Contest 2026
notes: The organizer's current rules publish exact 24-hour dates through 2029 and permit BPSK63 on 80, 40, 20, 15, and 10 metres. The listed frequencies are recommendations, not hard scoring limits. EU stations send a compact EU Area code and DX stations a progressive serial.

Both entrant groups score one point in the same DXCC entity, two within the same continent, and three between continents; a DX entrant scores five for an EU station. Maritime-mobile contacts score three and supply no multiplier. Every DXCC entity and every received EU Area count once per band, and the final score multiplies points by their sum.

The official PDF does not state a repeat-contact or duplicate rule, so SH6 does not invent one and retains rows, matching LogChecker in that narrow respect. SH6 validates compact alphabetic EU Area form but cannot prove membership in the organizer's date-versioned spreadsheet, and it cannot prove power, full-period operation, single-operator, single-signal, physical-location, or cross-log constraints; the rule is therefore partial.

rule_sets.name: ES Open HF Championship 2026
notes: ERAU's official 2026 rules define four one-hour tours on 18 April from 0500 through 0859 UTC, simultaneously on 80 and 40 metres. CW QSOs score two and SSB one. Every contact requires a continuous numeric serial; the published frequency ranges are recommendations rather than scoring limits.

An Estonian station may work every eligible station, while a non-Estonian entrant may work only Estonian stations. Contacts involving Russia or Belarus do not count. rule_sets.name: TRC DX Contest 2025

rule_sets.name: UBA DX Contest CW/SSB 2026
notes: Belgian entrants score one point for Belgium, two for one of the organizer-listed EU DXCC entities, and three otherwise.
